canonical_statement: For a satisfiable theory in a countable first-order language and a countable family of finite-arity partial types over the empty parameter set, each nonprincipal over the theory, there exists an at-most-countable model of the theory omitting every type.
domain_and_universes: L : Language.{u,v}; countable function and relation symbol types at every arity; T : L.Theory; Nat-indexed finite arities and formula sets; model carrier in max u v; Prop in universe 0
conclusion: There exists M : T.ModelType whose carrier is Countable and which omits p i for every i.

local_definitions.IsPartialType: The constants expansion of T union the formula set is finitely satisfiable.
local_definitions.Isolates: A formula is jointly satisfiable with T and T semantically entails its implication to every member of the type.
local_definitions.IsNonprincipal: No formula isolates the type over T.
local_definitions.Omits: Every tuple falsifies some member of the type.

killed: weakened omission of every realizing tuple to failure at one selected tuple

degenerate_cases: The Nat-indexed family permits repetitions; arity may vary and may be zero. Countable means at most countable, so finite models remain admissible. The empty family is represented by an extensionally empty Nat-indexed family rather than by changing the index type.
status_boundary: This freezes and elaborates the exact statement selected by intake. It supplies no omitting-types proof, source acceptance, anchor-audit, or downstream completion evidence.
